instruction: I prefer a darker, more subtle interface theme for VLC. Could you help me change the progress slider colors to a blackish theme to match my desktop environment better?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC slider colors to blackish theme. The evaluator checks the qt-slider-colours setting in VLC config file. Uses existing check_qt_slider_colours metric function with type='blackish' which validates that all RGB color values are below 100 (dark colors).
metadata.verification: Checked existing VLC metric functions. check_qt_slider_colours with type='blackish' parses the semicolon-separated RGB values and verifies all components are < 100, indicating dark colors.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vlc_config) correctly extracts VLC configuration file containing qt-slider-colours setting
Metric (check_qt_slider_colours) correctly parses semicolon-separated RGB values and validates all color components are < 100 (dark/blackish colors)
Complete coverage: instruction requires 'blackish theme' for slider colors, evaluator checks exactly this requirement
Appropriate postconfig: restarts VLC to ensure configuration changes are persisted to vlcrc file
Proper edge case handling: handles missing settings (uses default), file not found, and general exceptions
Data flow is correct: config file → extract qt-slider-colours → parse RGB values → validate darkness threshold
Parameter handling is correct: VLC metrics use 'rule' parameter name (consistent pattern), correctly accesses rule['type'] for 'blackish' validation
